blocks.text: Part B Standard Terms
1 Parties defined terms and contract documents

Company means Arasaka Inc. operating as Arman Arai. Client means each person identified in Part A. Event means the wedding and related coverage stated in Part A. Services and Deliverables mean only the items selected and specified in Part A.

The agreement consists of Part A, these Standard Terms, the accepted proposal identified in Part A, the signed privacy choice, every attached vendor or travel schedule and every later signed change order. If a document conflicts, a signed change order controls the issue it expressly changes, then Part A, then these Standard Terms, then the accepted proposal.
This agreement replaces earlier discussions about the same project except for a specific representation that applicable law does not permit the Company to exclude.
2 Booking reservation and payment
The Event date is reserved only when the Company receives a complete signed agreement and the booking payment stated in Part A. Until then, the date remains available to other clients.

The booking payment is credited to the Total Contract Price. Its cancellation treatment is governed by section 16, Part A and mandatory law. A label such as non-refundable does not override a statutory refund or cancellation right.

Invoices are payable on the exact dates stated in Part A. The Company may pause planning, editing or delivery while an undisputed payment is overdue after any notice or cure period required by law. The Company will not use a late fee or collection charge unless it is expressly stated, lawful and calculated as disclosed.
A chargeback does not itself cancel this agreement. The parties will first use the complaint and dispute process in section 22, without restricting any non-waivable chargeback or consumer right.
3 Scope planning and coordination

The Company will provide the selected services with reasonable care and skill. Creative planning may include consultations, schedule advice, location research, lighting and weather planning, coverage priorities and coordination with identified vendors.

Planning recommendations are not guarantees of vendor availability, permissions, weather, travel time, light, crowd levels or a particular visual result. Unless Part A states that the Company is the contracting party, clients select, contract with and pay vendors directly.

The final timeline is collaborative. Clients must approve a practical version by the deadline in Part A. A delay or schedule compression can reduce the images, audio, film scenes or group combinations reasonably achievable within the contracted coverage.
4 Third party vendors and substitutions

Part A must identify each material third party service, its legal supplier, price or allowance, contracting party and cancellation or substitution rule. The Company will disclose known vendor terms before booking and will not make a material substitution without written client approval except for an urgent same-day substitution reasonably necessary for safety or continuity.

When clients contract directly, the Company is not responsible for the third party's acts, omissions, insolvency, refusal, cancellation or legal compliance. The Company remains responsible for its own negligent recommendation or coordination to the extent imposed by law.
5 Travel accommodation and destination services

Travel, accommodation, transport, parking, permits, baggage, tolls and border costs are included only as itemized in Part A. Unless the Company confirms that it is lawfully supplying a travel service, clients contract with and pay airlines, hotels, carriers and other travel providers directly.

Clients are responsible for passports, visas, identification, venue access and lawful travel requirements applicable to them and their guests. The Company is responsible for its own required business travel documentation.
6 Coverage personnel and exclusivity

Coverage begins and ends at the exact times in Part A, including agreed travel between locations. Delays caused by clients, guests, venues, traffic, vendors or schedule changes do not automatically extend coverage. Overtime requires written approval and is charged using Part A.

The Company is not required to record every person, decoration, interaction or moment. Documentary coverage depends on access, timing, visibility, consent, venue restrictions, safety and competing events.

Clients will not engage another professional photographer or filmmaker to direct or cover the same contracted moments unless Part A permits it. Guests may take personal images if they do not materially obstruct, direct, light or delay the Company's work.
Arman Arai is the intended lead creator. The Company may use qualified employees, assistants and subcontractors under its direction. A replacement of the lead is governed by section 18.
7 Client cooperation guests and event information

Clients will provide accurate addresses, schedules, contacts, family group information, access rules, guest count, accessibility information affecting the plan, and any known safety or privacy restrictions by the stated deadlines.

Clients will appoint one decision contact who can make immediate timeline and group-photo decisions. The Company will make reasonable efforts to capture requested people and moments but cannot guarantee attendance, cooperation, punctuality, sobriety, visibility or uninterrupted access.

Clients are responsible for the conduct of their party and guests. Harassment, violence, dangerous intoxication, unlawful conduct, interference with equipment or repeated refusal to follow a reasonable safety direction may justify stopping coverage. The Company will document the reason and preserve any statutory rights.
8 Locations permits and venue rules

The party identified in Part A will obtain and pay for every required venue permission, commercial photography permit, park permit, drone authorization, access pass and insurance certificate. The Company will not trespass, breach a venue rule or misrepresent the nature of the work.

The Company will follow restrictions on flash, tripods, movement, ceremony access, audio recording, drone operation and commercial publication. These restrictions can limit the delivered material without constituting a service failure.
9 Safety weather health and accessibility

Safety overrides the planned image or film. The Company may stop, relocate, delay or modify work where a reasonable professional would consider conditions unsafe or unlawful, including severe weather, wildfire smoke, unsafe roads or water, wildlife, unstable structures, violence, intoxication or unsafe aviation conditions.

Clients will disclose only the mobility, pregnancy, medical, sensory or accessibility information reasonably necessary to plan pacing, access and emergency response. The Company will use that information only for the stated purpose and protect it as sensitive information.

Natural light, season, temperature, smoke, clouds, precipitation, venue lighting, road access and crowd levels are not guaranteed. The final dossier will state any alternate plan and decision threshold.
10 Photography film and audio capture
Clients reviewed the Company's portfolio and accept a consistent overall creative approach, not exact replication of another wedding, pose, colour palette, weather condition or background.

Photography coverage means professional still-image capture. Film coverage means selectively captured motion footage edited into the deliverables stated in Part A. It does not mean continuous multicamera recording unless Part A expressly says so.

Microphones and audio recorders may capture vows, officiant audio, speeches and ambient sound where lawful and permitted. Clients will notify speakers and participants when notice or consent is required. A venue or participant restriction may limit usable audio.

Drone capture is always conditional on aviation law, airspace, site permission, weather, visibility, crew qualification and safety. No refund is due solely because lawful and safe drone operation is unavailable unless Part A assigns a separate stated value or credit.
11 Editing selection and technical correction

The Company selects the photographs and footage that meet its professional and storytelling standards and applies its normal editing process, including exposure, colour, crop, sequencing, sound mixing, stabilization and reasonable blemish or distraction cleanup.

Duplicates, tests, misfires, closed eyes, unusable focus, accidental recordings and rejected or redundant material are not delivered. RAW photographs, unedited footage, project files, catalogues and source files are not delivered unless Part A expressly includes them.

Routine software-assisted denoising, masking, object cleanup, transcription, captioning and colour work may be used under the Company's supervision. The Company will not create a materially synthetic face, body, event or spoken statement and present it as documentary fact without informed written approval.

A technical defect is a failure to meet an objective specification in Part A. Creative preferences or requests beyond the contracted revision allowance are quoted as extra work. The Company will first have a reasonable opportunity to repair, replace or re-export an affected deliverable.
12 Delivery gallery access and archiving
Each delivery date, format, resolution, quantity or length and supply method appears in Part A. A stated range is an estimate within that range, not a promise of the maximum.

The online gallery remains available for the period stated in Part A. Clients must download and maintain at least two separate backups before expiry. Reactivation is not guaranteed and may require the disclosed fee if the files still exist.

The Company may retain working files for the period stated in the delivery guide for service recovery, legal and business continuity. It may securely delete files after that period subject to legal holds and applicable privacy law. The Company will not promise indefinite archive storage.

Delivery is complete when the agreed files are made available by the stated secure method or shipped to the approved address. Physical goods risk transfers as provided by applicable sale-of-goods and consumer law.
13 Albums prints and physical goods
An album or physical product is supplied only if selected in Part A. Size, materials, page count, proof rounds, shipping, production estimate and client deadlines must be specified before production.

Clients must review every name, date, caption, crop, image and layout. Final written proof approval authorizes manufacture of that exact version. The Company remains responsible for manufacturing defects and for matching the approved proof within reasonable production tolerances.
14 Copyright client licence and moral rights

Copyright in the Company's photographs, films, edits and original creative work remains with Arasaka Inc. or the identified creator subject to any written assignment. Payment does not transfer copyright or source files.

After full payment, clients receive a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to download, store, display, print and share the delivered files for personal and non-commercial purposes. Commercial publication, paid promotion, resale, sublicensing, contest entry on behalf of a business, or third-party licensing requires prior written permission unless law provides otherwise.

Clients may make ordinary personal crops and size adjustments but will not apply misleading filters, AI face or body replacement, or another edit that materially misrepresents the Company's work when crediting the Company. Copyright ownership does not override each person's privacy or publicity choice.
15 Privacy and personal information

Arman Arai is the privacy contact unless Part A identifies another person. The Company collects only information reasonably necessary to quote, contract, plan, deliver, secure, invoice, insure, archive and support the services, and to satisfy legal obligations.

Optional portfolio, testimonial, advertising and marketing use requires the separate privacy and publicity form. Refusing optional consent does not change price, priority, creative effort or delivery. A client cannot grant publicity consent for another identifiable adult or for a minor whose lawful guardian has not consented.

The Company may use service providers for gallery hosting, storage, payment, communication, editing, album production and professional advice. It will use reasonable contractual and technical safeguards and provide cross-border processing notice where applicable.

A person may request access, correction or withdrawal of optional consent by contacting the privacy contact. Withdrawal does not invalidate prior lawful use and may be subject to reasonable processing time, legal retention and materials already irreversibly printed or distributed.
16 Client cancellation
Clients may cancel by clear written notice to the notice address in Part A. Cancellation takes effect when the Company receives the notice. Any statutory cancellation right applies first.

If no statutory cancellation right changes the result, the cancellation amount is the reasonable portion of the Total Contract Price stated in Part A or the attached schedule, reflecting date reservation, completed work, committed non-recoverable third-party costs and the Company's reasonable mitigation. It is not intended as a penalty.

The booking payment is credited against the lawful cancellation amount. The Company will refund any excess within the period required by law, or otherwise within 15 calendar days after the amount is determined and returned third-party funds are received. Clients remain responsible for approved non-recoverable third-party costs identified before commitment.

blocks.text: 17 Client requested rescheduling and scope changes

A requested date change is not effective until both sides sign a change order. The Company may accept a new date within the period stated in Part A, subject to availability and the reasonable cost of the change.

If the Company is unavailable for the proposed date, clients may keep the original date and scope, accept a qualified replacement under section 18, or cancel under section 16 unless a statutory or signed term produces a different result.

A material location, guest count, route, venue, timeline, personnel, service or deliverable change may affect price, taxes, permits, travel, staffing, deadlines and the cancellation calculation. The Company will provide a written change order before acting whenever reasonably possible.
18 Company unavailability

If Arman Arai cannot personally perform because of serious illness, injury, emergency or another cause beyond reasonable control, the Company will promptly notify clients and offer a reasonably comparable qualified replacement where available.

Clients may accept the replacement. If the proposed replacement materially changes the contracted creative service, clients may reject it and receive a refund for the unperformed Company services, subject to any greater mandatory remedy. Approved third-party services already supplied remain payable.
19 Force majeure and external interruption

A force majeure event is an event beyond reasonable control that prevents or makes illegal a material obligation, including government closure, severe disaster, wildfire evacuation, border closure, war, civil emergency, sudden venue destruction, transportation shutdown, serious infrastructure failure or another comparable event.

The affected party will notify the other promptly, explain the impact and take reasonable steps to reduce loss. The parties will first consider rescheduling, lawful alternatives, substitute performance and recoverable third-party credits. Nothing in this section excludes a statutory cancellation or refund right.
20 Equipment data loss and service remedies

The Company will use commercially reasonable equipment, backup practices, media handling and data protection appropriate to professional wedding coverage. Equipment, media, storage and network failures can still occur despite reasonable care.

For a partial loss or material technical failure that cannot reasonably be repaired, clients may choose a proportionate re-performance where feasible, a proportionate refund based on the affected contracted service or deliverable, or another agreed remedy. The limitation below does not apply to fraud, wilful misconduct, gross negligence, death or bodily injury caused by negligence, or a remedy that law does not permit the Company to limit.

Subject to those exceptions, the Company's total monetary liability arising from this agreement will not exceed the Total Contract Price actually paid or payable for the affected project. Neither party is liable for indirect or special loss that was not reasonably foreseeable when the agreement was made.
21 Responsibility and indemnity

Each party is responsible for loss caused by its breach, negligence or unlawful conduct. A client indemnity applies only to third-party claims caused by material supplied by that client, instructions that infringe another person's rights, or that client's unlawful conduct, and only to the extent the claim was not caused by the Company's own breach or negligence.
No settlement may impose an admission, non-monetary obligation or reputation statement on another party without that party's written consent.
22 Complaints consumer rights and dispute resolution

Clients should report a concern to the notice email with the affected date, file or service and requested resolution. The Company will acknowledge the complaint within five business days and provide a substantive response within a reasonable time based on the issue.

The parties will first attempt direct resolution and may voluntarily use mediation. A requirement to negotiate or mediate does not prevent urgent court relief, a chargeback, a regulator complaint, a statutory consumer remedy or access to a court or tribunal that applicable law protects.

The law of the province or territory selected in Part A governs to the extent that choice is lawful. Mandatory consumer, privacy and other protections applicable to a client or place of supply remain unaffected. Any permitted court proceeding will be brought in a court with lawful jurisdiction.
23 General terms

Neither party may assign the agreement without the other's written consent except that the Company may assign receivables or transfer the agreement with substantially all of the relevant business if the transfer does not materially reduce client rights.

A waiver applies only to the specific instance written and does not waive later enforcement. If a provision is invalid or unenforceable, it will be read down or severed only to the minimum extent necessary and the rest continues.

The agreement may be signed in counterparts and by an electronic method that applicable law recognizes. A signer confirms the opportunity to review, correct errors, save or print the completed agreement and receive an executed copy.

Headings assist reading and do not narrow the text. Including means including without limitation. A business day excludes Saturdays, Sundays and statutory holidays in the governing province unless Part A states otherwise.
24 Notices and cancellation delivery

A notice under this agreement may be delivered personally, by traceable mail or by email to the addresses in Part A and is effective as provided by applicable law. A client cancellation notice must clearly identify the agreement and state the intention to cancel. No special form is required unless mandatory law requires one.

blocks.text: Part B Terms
1 Performance and direction

The contractor will perform the assigned services with reasonable professional care, arrive ready at the stated call time and follow the lead's lawful creative, safety, privacy and venue instructions. The contractor has no authority to change client scope, promise deliverables, collect client payment or bind the Company.

The contractor will immediately report delay, illness, equipment failure, card or file error, safety issue, venue restriction, client complaint or conflict. The contractor will not abandon the assignment without an emergency or lead approval.
2 Client contact and professional conduct

The contractor will communicate respectfully, dress appropriately for the stated event, avoid intoxication and harassment, and not use the assignment to solicit clients or vendors. Client contact after the event is limited to communication authorized by the Company.
The contractor will not publish names, locations, schedules, images, audio or behind-the-scenes material without the Company's written permission and the required participant consent.
3 Privacy confidentiality and security

Client identities, contact details, schedules, family relationships, health or accessibility information, security plans, pricing and unpublished media are confidential. The contractor will access only what is required for the assignment and will not copy it to personal cloud, messaging or AI services unless approved.

The contractor will use secure devices, current access controls and reasonable media handling. A lost device, copied credential, misdirected message or suspected privacy breach must be reported to the Company immediately with all available facts.
4 Media custody and delivery

The contractor will label and protect every card, drive and recorder according to the production plan. Original media must be delivered to the Company by the stated time and method. The contractor will not format, erase, overwrite or reuse media until the Company confirms verified receipt and authorizes release.

If the contractor uses personal media or devices, the contractor will maintain one secure copy until the Company confirms two verified copies, then securely delete remaining client material when instructed, subject to legal retention.
5 Copyright assignment and moral rights

In consideration of the assignment fee, the contractor assigns to Arasaka Inc. all worldwide copyright and related rights the contractor owns in photographs, footage, recordings, edits and other work created specifically for this assignment, effective on creation. To the extent an assignment requires further documentation, the contractor will sign it reasonably promptly.

The contractor waives in favour of Arasaka Inc. and its authorized licensees all moral rights in the assigned work to the extent Canadian law permits waiver. The contractor retains ownership of pre-existing tools, presets and general know-how but grants the Company the licence needed to use them as embedded in the assigned work.
No portfolio use is granted to the contractor unless the Company gives written permission identifying the files, timing, credit and permitted channels after checking the clients' privacy choice.
6 Compensation tax and status

The Company will pay accepted services and approved expenses as stated in Part A after receiving the required invoice and media. The contractor is responsible for its own tax registrations, remittances and business expenses except as Part A states.

The parties intend the status recorded in Part A, but labels do not override the actual relationship or mandatory law. Nothing prevents a regulator, tax authority, workers compensation board or court from determining the legal status from the facts.
7 Cancellation replacement and inability to perform

blocks.text: 8 Liability and remedies

Each party is responsible for loss caused by its breach, negligence or unlawful conduct. The contractor will have a reasonable opportunity to explain or cure a correctable file, delivery or invoice issue. Neither party excludes liability that law does not permit it to exclude.
9 General terms
